name: Habana Gaudi PyTorch Bridge and the Gaudi torch fork (torch-hpu)
notable_features: This IS the Gaudi PyTorch. The Gaudi fork does not live in a PyTorch mirror you can pick from - it is assembled by this bridge repo's scripts/install_torch_fork.sh, which downloads a prebuilt torch wheel whose version is dictated by the Habana installer

The version-locking is the design. install_torch_fork.sh takes two arguments, VERSION and BUILD, and the documented way to obtain them is to parse the output of habanalabs-installer.sh -v. So the PyTorch you run is a function of which Gaudi software stack release you installed, not of what PyTorch you want

'Several Python packages enabling Intel Gaudi functionality in PyTorch with minimal code changes' - the bridge's own framing, and the 'minimal code changes' refers to model code: the framework-level difference is what this record is about
Same release also provides habana-media-loader, pinned to the identical VERSION.BUILD string, so the dataloader cannot be versioned separately from the framework either

Ships a GAUDI-OPTIMIZATION layer rather than leaving it to the user: the repo's own optimization guide ([[xpu-habana-optimization-guide]]) documents MPI CPU binding (--bind-to core --map-by socket:PE=6, six cores per Gaudi on an HLS-1 with 96 CPUs and 8 devices), setting the CPU governor to performance, and Gaudi-3-specific BIOS and MSR work (Energy Perf BIAS, HWP core frequency, disabling SubNUMA and C6, Latency Optimized Mode). This is a genuine hardware-first obligation: on Gaudi you tune the host CPU, which no portable engine asks you to do
19 stars, 9 forks, 5 open issues, Apache-2.0, created 2024-09-29, last push 2026-07-13, NOT archived
hardware_caveats: Not actually a portable PyTorch. torch-hpu is a fork pinned to a Gaudi software stack release, so 'what PyTorch version is this' has no independent answer - it is (Gaudi release, PyTorch release) as a pair, and the vLLM plugin compounds this with a third number (vLLM version). See [[vllm-gaudi]]

The build writes into SYSTEM directories: it requires sudo chmod +xw /usr/lib/habanalabs and a manual symlink of hl_logger headers into /usr/include/habanalabs. This breaks clean-install and container immutability assumptions in a way that no pip-installable portable framework does
Assumed build host is Ubuntu 22.04; the README says other operating systems require adjusting the package steps
Underlying compiler is closed. The bridge is the open shell; the actual Gaudi compiler is SynapseAI, which is only partially open - see [[xpu-synapseai]] for exactly how little of it is
Star count of 19 with 9 forks signals a vendor-internal repo published for reference rather than a community-maintained one; expect low community support volume
Because torch-hpu is a fork, upstream PyTorch fixes arrive only when the Gaudi team rebases. There is no mechanism in the bridge README that would make that fast
best_for: Running existing PyTorch inference code on Gaudi with minimal model-code edits
Understanding what a hardware-first framework fork actually costs in version coupling and system-level install steps
Anyone tuning Gaudi throughput, since the host-CPU and BIOS prerequisites in the linked optimization guide are mandatory rather than optional
avoid_for: Environments where the system has to be reproducible from a lockfile alone - the version triple cannot be derived without running the Habana installer
Assuming upstream PyTorch behaviour. Fork lag is invisible until it bites
notes: The repo already documents the Gaudi compiler's static-shape and graph-capture behaviour as flops records ([[xpu-gaudi-static-shapes]], [[xpu-gaudi-hpu-graphs]], [[xpu-gaudi-fusion-pass]]) and the Gaudi serving path as [[vllm-gaudi]]; this record covers the layer in between - the framework fork itself - so it does not duplicate the constraint mechanics.
